text: Welcome to the build. Each of the six stages is a small function in the churn project, and every result you see came from a real local run.

Stage one trains and tracks. One function starts an MLflow run, fits the pipeline, logs the parameters and metrics, and saves the model. The store is a plain folder on disk, so there is no server to set up. We got a ROC A U C of point seven four four and an average precision of point three three three.

Stage two is the gate, a pure function that takes metrics and returns a verdict with reasons. The baseline passes. A weak candidate with an A U C of point six two is blocked for missing the floor. And a candidate at point seven two clears the floor but is blocked because it is worse than the champion. Because it is a plain function, it is easy to unit test.

Stage three registers, and then promotes. Registering creates version one, but the champion alias still points nowhere. Only promote moves the alias, so we can test a version before anyone can serve it.

Stage four serves the model with Python's standard library and tests the contract over real H T T P requests. A valid customer returns a probability of point seven three seven and the model version. An unknown plan, or a missing field, returns a four twenty two with a clear message.

Stages five and six run weekly. In week two, nothing alarms. In week four, days idle reaches a P S I of point eight six seven, and the alarm fires. The retrain decision then answers hold, investigate, wait, or retrain, from the same settings file.
Finally, the cycle runs in a careful order: train and gate, register, contract test, and only then promote. A failure at any step stops the cycle, and the champion is untouched.
Next, we run the entire lifecycle and try to break it.
